symptoms: The job fails before any stage runs -- the plan was never built
The message names a table or a column
The same code worked against another catalog or another environment
likely_causes: The table or the column the query names does not exist in the catalog the session resolved
The session resolved a different catalog than the author assumed, so the name points elsewhere
The schema of the table changed and the query still names the old column
diagnostic_steps: Read the schema of the table the query names, from the catalog dump, and compare column by column with what the query projects
Read which catalog the session resolved: a name that resolves in one catalog and not in another is a catalog problem, not a schema one
Separate the two halves of the message: a missing TABLE and a missing COLUMN have different causes and different fixes
fixes: Correct the name the query uses, when the catalog shows the object under another name
Point the session at the catalog where the object lives
Update the query to the current schema when a column was renamed or dropped
unsafe_fixes: Recreating the table to make the name resolve, which loses the data that was there
Disabling schema enforcement so the read stops complaining, which moves the failure to the consumer
verification: Re-run and confirm the plan builds. Then compare the output schema with the expected one: a query that resolves is not yet a query that returns the right columns
rollback: Restore the previous query text. If the fix changed the schema of a table, the rollback is of data and the consumers have to be inventoried first
